title: Translating Harder Quantified Sentences
short: Handle "only", "none but", "all except", complex subjects (red cars) and complex predicates (fast or loud) inside one quantifier.
trouble: Learners translate "Only S are P" as ∀x(Sx → Px). It is ∀x(Px → Sx): everything that is P is S.

blocks.html: Real sentences add words to the four basic forms of Translating A, E, I and O: adjectives on the subject, two properties in the predicate, "only", "none but" and "all except" from Only, None But and All Except. The method stays the same: find the form, then translate the subject phrase and the predicate phrase as whole pieces.

head: English
Symbols
rows: $S$ and $Q$ are $P$ (cats and dogs are pets).

blocks.html: Translate the subject phrase into one condition (an adjective adds $\land$) and the predicate phrase into another, then join them with $\to$ under $\forall$ or $\land$ under $\exists$. "Only $S$ are $P$" reverses the order: $\forall x(Px \to Sx)$.

"Only members may vote" does not say every member votes; it says anyone who votes is a member. The word after "only" names a necessary condition, and a necessary condition goes after the arrow, just as with "only if" in Translating Conditionals. "Cats and dogs are pets" uses "and" in English, but no single thing is both a cat and a dog; the sentence means anything that is a cat or a dog is a pet.

blocks.name: lg-quantworld
blocks.cap: "Only circles and triangles are red" is the first sentence; "all circles are red" the second.

blocks.title: Only
blocks.q: Let $Mx$: $x$ is a member; $Vx$: $x$ votes. Translate "Only members vote."
steps: Anyone who votes is a member.

blocks.title: An adjective
blocks.q: Let $Bx$: $x$ is a bird; $Yx$: $x$ is young; $Fx$: $x$ can fly. Translate "Some young birds can fly."
steps: Subject: things that are young and birds.
Something is a young bird and can fly.

blocks.title: A compound subject
blocks.q: Let $Cx$: cat; $Dx$: dog; $Px$: pet. Translate "Cats and dogs are pets."
steps: Anything that is a cat or a dog is a pet.

blocks.html: Translating "Only $S$ are $P$" as $\forall x(Sx \to Px)$. That says every $S$ is a $P$, which is a different claim: "only members vote" does not mean every member votes. Put the word after "only" behind the arrow: $\forall x(Px \to Sx)$.

blocks.title: All except
blocks.q: In a club, let $Mx$: $x$ is a manager; $Px$: $x$ pays dues. Translate "All except managers pay dues."
steps: Two claims: everyone who is not a manager pays dues, and no manager pays dues.
Join the two universal statements with $\land$.

blocks.html: When a sentence feels tangled, rewrite it in "logician's English" first: "for any $x$, if $x$ is a young bird, then $x$ can fly." Once the English has that shape, the symbols follow almost word for word.
